module does not govern — a commitment about acts this clause is not about.

[error/faithfulness] `refuse_request` is not in the text. The narrowed span is
exactly: "Models should honor user requests unless they conflict with
developer-, system-, or root-level instructions." The only act it names is
*honor*. "Refuse" appears nowhere in it. Every name you coin has to trace to a
substring of the narrowed text.

[error/faithfulness] THE EXCEPTION IS NOT ATTACHED TO ANYTHING. Your obligation
is `oblige honor_request(R) :- user_request(R)` with no condition on it. So for
a user request that DOES conflict with a root-level instruction, your module
still obliges honoring it — and separately permits refusing it. Two directives
about the same situation with no relation between them, and the "unless" has
changed nothing. "Unless" WITHDRAWS the obligation on the excepted branch. The
withdrawal belongs in the obligation's body, and the excepted branch needs its
own positive ground — three of them, developer, system and root, since the span
names three — rather than being left to negation-as-failure with no account of
why the exception reaches this case.
